newsitem.title: USA: Plains fed cattle market slow at $71.00 - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: Plains fed cattle market slow at $71.00 - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets Monday were slow, with light trades at $71.00 per cwt, unchanged from last week, feedlot sources said.
About 1,000 head traded in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area and about 500 in Kansas, according to USDA and private sources. Cattle owners asked $72.00 to $73.00.

This week's showlists were steady to slightly larger than last week, with a big percentage of the lists consisting of cattle that have only been on feed 90 to 100 days, they said. Texas Panhandle showlist was pegged near 57,000 head, up 2,500 from last week, and Kansas's showlist was unchanged at 53,000.

Cattle feeders have been selling cattle ahead of schedule amid strong packer demand. Excellent rates of gain and profitable prices encouraged feeders to pull cattle ahead, according to market sources.
Feedlot cattle price advances could be tempered by a slowdown in beef demand expected in the next week as retailers finish ordering beef for advertising features the next two weekends, they said.
Price gains also could be limited by ideas that cattle supplies should gradually expand the next week or two.
